I need to understand the full picture of bugs.

Project filtering hides status changes, comments, and comment edits/deletions. Status changes and comments have `projectId: null`. Comment edits and deletions are not subscribed to.

The expected behavior is that project filtering should include all related entries. Status changes and comments need their projectId set correctly. The comment.created event payload does not contain a projectId field.

There is no `comment.updated` event. I need to either add `projectId` to the comment payload or look up the issue to determine the project. The instructions require every workspace action to appear exactly once and carry its project.

I should check the event emitters to see if projectId is available when emitting comment events. I also need to look for a comment.updated event.

The `issue.assigned` listener incorrectly uses `payload.assigneeId` as the actor. It should use `payload.actorId` instead, since the EventEnvelope carries the correct assigner.

Several actions never appear in the feed at all. These include issue edits and archives, project edits and restores, member joins and leaves, and feature flag toggles.

The listener map is missing subscriptions for issue.updated, issue.archived, comment.updated, comment.deleted, member.joined, member.removed, and flag.toggled. The project.restored event exists but has no listener.

The member.joined and member.removed events exist but have no listeners. The flag.toggled event also exists without a listener. Some activity actions like organization.updated, project.updated, and issue.restored appear to lack corresponding event types entirely.

The `record()` function stamps every entry with the current time instead of the event's original `occurredAt`. A background catch-up job can then misplace entries under the wrong date, and time-range filters will miss them entirely. The fix is to use the event payload's `occurredAt` directly.

The export endpoint is capped at 100 entries per call. It also uses an exclusive `until` filter, so any activity that occurs exactly at the cutoff timestamp is omitted. The fix requires paginating through all results and switching the boundary to an inclusive check.

The export endpoint must also reject ranges where the end time is before the start time. The JSON export used to include entry details such as old and new status values, but those fields are now empty.
